newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FORECAST - Vienna ATX seen racing to 1,250 points.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Vienna ATX seen racing to 1,250 points.

text.p: Investmentbank Austria said on Wednesday Austria's blue-chip ATX index could rise to 1,250 points within the next few months, helped by an increase in liquidity, but warned the bull run may be over soon afterwards.

"The ATX should reach a range of 1,200 to 1,250 points in the first few months of the year. After that, blue chips will be in for a correction of between five and ten percent," Fritz Schweiger, the bank's chief analyst, told a news conference.
The ATX stood at 1,181.21 in the last half hour of trading on the Vienna stock exchange on Wednesday.
Schweiger said low interest rates and tame inflation should prevail in 1997, and that the prospect of rising corporate earnings should continue to boost liquidity.
Earnings of ATX member companies were expected to rise by 10.6 percent this year, and by 14.6 percent in 1998, he said.
The ATX rose by 18.8 percent over the course of last year.
Despite the strong increase, Investmentbank Austria said the market was neither overheated nor overvalued.
"Price/earnings ratios are low compared with other European countries," Schweiger said, forecasting a ratio of 14.8 for the current year and of 12.6 for 1998.
But the analyst warned the positive outlook was clouded by two major risk factors.

"If the upswing in the economy is to weak, we will see lower corporate earnings and a correction. If the economy is booming, we would probably see some interest rate hikes. In this case the market could drop by up to 15 percent", Schweiger said.

The bank, a subsidiary of market leader Bank Austria, said it recommended shares such as technology group VA Technologie, steel makers VA Stahl and Boehler-Uddeholm, utility EVN, fire-proof materials maker Radex-Heraklith and brick maker Wienerberger as buys.
Schweiger added insurer Wiener Staedtische remained one of Europe's best valued insurance stocks.
